summary: AI observability gives teams visibility into how LLM applications behave in production, surfacing latency, token usage, quality, and cost data that would otherwise remain opaque. As LLM calls grow in volume and expense, tracing, evaluation, and cost monitoring become essential for debugging failures, controlling spend, and maintaining output quality. The right observability stack turns unpredictable AI systems into measurable, optimizable ones.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces, LLM/chain/agent executions, token usage, latency, cost, and evaluation metrics—tightly integrated with the LangChain ecosystem.
features: Distributed tracing with span hierarchies for chains and agents
tools.pricing: Free tier includes ~5,000 monthly traces. Beyond the allowance, base traces (14-day retention) cost $2.50 per 1k and extended traces (400-day retention) cost $5.00 per 1k. Paid Plus plans and enterprise tiers available.
tools.best_for: Teams building on LangChain/LangGraph who want deeply integrated tracing, evaluation, and debugging.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests via a proxy or async logging—tracks cost, token usage, latency, request/response payloads, caching, and rate limits.
features: One-line proxy integration for logging and caching
Cost and usage analytics per model, user, and request
Caching and rate limiting to reduce spend
tools.pricing: Free tier includes up to 10,000 monthly traces. Pro at $79/month (approx. $79 per 100,000 traces), Team at $799/month, plus custom enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting lightweight, provider-agnostic cost tracking and caching with minimal code changes.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompts, evaluations, and model experiments through W&B Weave—plus broader ML experiment tracking, datasets, and model performance.
features: Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
Integration with the full MLOps lifecycle
tools.pricing: Free personal tier for individuals. Team and Enterprise plans are usage/seat-based with custom pricing; contact sales for volume rates.
tools.best_for: ML teams that want unified LLM observability alongside traditional experiment tracking and model management.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production LLM and ML model performance—traces, embeddings, drift, hallucination/quality metrics, and evaluation at scale.
features: LLM tracing and span-level observability (Phoenix OSS)
tools.pricing: Open-source Phoenix is free and self-hosted. Arize AX offers a free tier with paid Pro and Enterprise plans priced by volume and features (contact sales).
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing rigorous production monitoring, evaluation, and drift detection across LLM and ML workloads.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, token usage, cost, latency, prompt versions, and evaluation scores—open-source and framework-agnostic.
features: Open-source, self-hostable tracing with span hierarchies
Cost and usage analytics per model
tools.pricing: Free and open-source if self-hosted. Managed cloud offers a free Hobby tier, Core/Pro plans (~$29–$199/month), and Enterprise pricing based on usage.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, vendor-neutral observability platform with full control via self-hosting.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM traces, token usage, latency, and cost through OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation that exports to any OTel-compatible backend.
features: Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM providers and frameworks
Vendor-neutral export to existing observability backends
Span-level traces for LLM calls and chains
Easy integration with Traceloop, Datadog, Grafana, etc.
tools.pricing: Free and open-source. Traceloop's managed cloud (the maintainer) offers a free tier plus paid plans based on event volume.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting standards-based, OpenTelemetry-native instrumentation that plugs into existing observability infrastructure.

cost_tips: Cache repeated or similar requests (e.g., via Helicone or a semantic cache) so identical prompts don't trigger redundant paid API calls.
Route to the smallest capable model and reserve expensive frontier models for genuinely complex tasks—use model tiering and prompt-complexity routing.
Trim token usage by shortening prompts, summarizing or truncating context, and limiting max output tokens to only what's needed.
Monitor cost per request, user, and feature with observability dashboards to catch runaway usage, then set budgets and alerts to prevent surprise bills.
